description:
We are Cosmic Duo, a passionate team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our journey with NASA Space Apps began in 2025, when our previous project earned us the recognition of Global Nominee, placing us among the outstanding teams in the challenge.

Our interests include space technology, Mars exploration, robotics, embedded systems, software development, and interactive game design
summary:
We developed Earth Jukebox, an interactive web-based acoustic observatory that translates NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations into real-time, musically structured soundscapes.
Using browser-side computer vision and the Web Audio API, the application scans visual frames across longitude, latitude, or temporal evolution sequences—converting pixel luminance, warm-to-cool color gradients, and high-contrast transients into four synchronized synthesis stems: a Thermal Pad, Density Bells, Transient Sparkles, and Planetary Bass, quantized to selectable harmonic scales. Users can explore six curated NASA-inspired Earth datasets or upload custom satellite imagery and video frames, probe specific coordinates by pointer, inspect live frequencies via a D3.js FFT overlay, and export both stereo WAV audio and multi-track MIDI files for DAW production.
By pairing non-speech audio synthesis with keyboard navigation, spoken scene guides, and live visual feedback, Earth Jukebox makes complex climate and planetary science accessible to blind and low-vision audiences while offering everyone an intuitive, multi-sensory way to experience how Earth is changing.
details:
Earth Jukebox is an interactive, web-based acoustic observatory that transforms NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations into real-time musical soundscapes. The project aims to make complex Earth science data more engaging, accessible, and easier to experience through sound.

The application uses browser-side computer vision to analyze NASA's Earth visualization frames across longitude, latitude, and temporal sequences. It translates visual properties such as pixel luminance, warm-to-cool colour gradients, and high-contrast changes into four synchronized audio synthesis layers: Thermal Pad, Density Bells, Transient Sparkles, and additional sound elements. Using the Web Audio API, these layers combine to generate evolving musical compositions that reflect changes in Earth's environmental data.

The key benefit of Earth Jukebox is its ability to provide an alternative, multisensory way of understanding scientific visualizations. Instead of relying entirely on charts, maps, and numerical representations, users can listen to patterns and changes in Earth data, making scientific exploration more immersive and interactive. Its intended impact is to encourage curiosity about our planet, improve public engagement with Earth science, and introduce creative approaches to scientific data interpretation.

Technologies Used: NASA Earth Information Center visualizations, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, browser-side computer vision, and Web Audio API for real-time audio synthesis and sound generation.

The creativity of Earth Jukebox lies in connecting two seemingly different fields: Earth science and music. It transforms environmental information into an auditory experience, where visual changes directly influence musical characteristics. During development, our team considered scientific relevance, the relationship between visual data and sound, real-time responsiveness, synchronization of audio layers, user experience, accessibility, and the balance between scientific representation and musical creativity.

Ultimately, Earth Jukebox demonstrates how technology, science, and creativity can come together to turn Earth's data into an interactive musical experience.
